<meta>continues from previous page: so that</meta> from then on its powers, namely for expelling, may be rendered stronger; and furthermore, that the doses of precipitated Mercury <note>original: "Mercurij præcipitati"; a chemical preparation of mercury used as a purgative</note> may be more easily formed for administration or absorption, specifically in the form of pills. Here, therefore, precipitated Mercury is uniquely praised and recommended, and indeed it is very effective. The Mercury of Life <term>Mercurius vitæ</term> <gloss>antimony oxychloride, a potent emetic and purgative</gloss> or the Flowers of Butter of Antimony, of which we spoke above, accomplishes the same if 4 to 12 grains are administered for three full days in an extract of Hellebore and Bitter Apple <term>colocynthis</term> <gloss>a powerful purgative fruit</gloss>; it expels the resolved salt <note>the dissolved minerals or humors causing the fluid retention</note> quite successfully. Afterward, however, sweating and urination should be moved with a decoction of sarsaparilla, Holy Wood <term>ligni sancti</term> <gloss>Guaiacum, known for its resinous medicinal properties</gloss>, or asarum root, always adding Spirit of Tartar <note>a potassium-based distillate used as a diuretic</note> or other diaphoretics <gloss>sweat-inducing agents</gloss> and diuretics, of which we spoke above. Especially, however, adding the secret essence <term>arcanum</term> of wormwood or blessed thistle. It must be noted here, however, that the three-day administration of the Mercury of Life in adults often tends to cause a prolapse of the anus, which afterward is cured only rarely or with great difficulty. In treating dropsy <term>hydrops</term> <gloss>an old term for edema or fluid swelling</gloss>, it is necessary that such purgatives be applied immediately from the beginning of the cure; afterward, diuretics and hydrotics <note>medicines that promote the discharge of water</note> should follow. Otherwise, a reversal of order <term>ὕστερον πρότερον</term> <gloss>the latter before the former</gloss> would be practiced here; all the serum or water would be rolled down to the kidneys and ureters, where afterward, on account of the burden, very stubborn symptoms often tend to arise. Furthermore, in the preparation of the extract of Black Hellebore root, it is safer to take the wine itself instead of Spirit of Wine <note>pure alcohol</note>, with which the root itself should be gently boiled without loud bubbling, and this should be done with fresh wine for as long as it takes until all the essential power has been extracted from the roots; afterward, by evaporating or distilling to the thickness of honey, it should be reduced to an extract. <summary>Crollius describes the chemical preparation of purgatives and diuretics, specifically Mercury of Life and Hellebore, to treat dropsy by first purging the body before stimulating fluid expulsion to avoid organ strain.</summary>
